name: BASS - Burning and Suppression of Solids
hardware: MSG (ISS)
key_findings: NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is not conservative; materials burn at lower O2 in microgravity; a local nitrogen jet can strengthen the flame
Burning and extinction of solids; improve 1 g safety tests and extinction strategies
modifications: Revise NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 (upward burning in 1 g) because it underestimates flammability in microgravity at low flows (~1-10 cm/s)
Prohibit applying slow localized N2 jets directly at the flame base without first cutting HVAC ventilation, since entrained O2 intensifies the fire

name: BASS-II - Burning and Suppression of Solids II
hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / modified SPICE flow duct (7.6 x 7.6 cm section)
key_findings: PMMA and SIBAL fabric samples sustain stable faint blue flames at ultra-low flows (0.5-2 cm/s) with O2 concentrations up to 2.5-3.5% below the 1 g terrestrial limit; stepping the fan down (step-down flow) reveals thermal hysteresis before radiative extinction
Determine flame spread rates (Vf), radiative extinction limits (low flow) and convective blowoff limits (high flow), and compare the limiting oxygen index (MOC) in 0 g with NASA-STD-6001 Test 1
modifications: Lower the MOC certification threshold for cabin polymers and textiles to <= 15.0% O2 for slow-ventilation regimes (0.5-8 cm/s)
Add two-branch extinction curves (radiative quenching < 1 cm/s and convective blowoff > 30 cm/s) to the Orion/Gateway fire code
Require a waiting time after ventilation shutoff (> 60 s) because of the thermal inertia of thick solids (PMMA >= 3.2 mm)

name: PSI-68: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2 (FLEX-2) in the ISS CIR / MDCA
hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
key_findings: Large linear alkanes (n-heptane, n-decane, n-dodecane) undergo radiative extinction of the visible hot flame but keep vaporizing through invisible cool flames governed by NTC (negative temperature coefficient) chemistry, which can produce an explosive vapour-cloud reignition; in alcohols (methanol/ethanol), absorption of the water produced in the flame causes abrupt extinction

Quantify the burning-rate constant K (d^2 law: D^2 = D0^2 - K*t), soot-shell formation, radiative extinction of the hot flame, transition to two-stage combustion (cool flames at 550-750 K) and droplet-droplet interaction
modifications: Integrate low-temperature kinetic sub-mechanisms (NTC / RO2 alkyl peroxides) into space propulsion and safety CFD models to predict cool flames (550-750 K)
Install UV (OH* at 310 nm) + UV/visible (HCHO* at 395 nm) and IR optical diagnostics in combustion chambers and habitats
Raise the CO2/N2 dilution margin by at least +4% to suppress both the hot-flame and cool-flame branches in heavy hydrocarbons

name: LUCI (Lunar-g Combustion Investigation) & FM2 (Flammability of Materials on the Moon) - Efecto Goldilocks y Escala de de Ris en 0.16g
hardware: Centrífuga de caída libre NASA GRC / Cohete Sonda LUCI / Payload autónomo lunar CLPS FM2 / SoFIE (ISS MSG)
key_findings: Efecto 'Goldilocks' en la Luna (0.16g): en 1-g la fuerte flotabilidad (~20-30 cm/s) enfría y apaga la llama (blowoff), mientras en 0-g falta oxígeno sin ventilación; en cambio, en 0.16g la flotabilidad natural induce ~6.8-7.5 cm/s (justo en el mínimo de la curva LOI en U), haciendo que los materiales ardan a menor O2 en la Luna (LOI ~ 13.7-14.5% O2) que en la Tierra (LOI ~ 16.5-18.0% O2)
Cuantificar el Índice Límite de Oxígeno (LOI en forma de U) y la velocidad de propagación de llama según la escala de de Ris en gravedad lunar (0.16g) frente a 0-g y 1-g
modifications: Reemplazar la certificación terrestre NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 (1-g) por ensayos o factores de corrección en el mínimo de la curva LOI en U (flujo equivalente de 6.5-8.0 cm/s para 0.16g lunar)
Incorporar en el motor de predicción la velocidad boyante intrínseca V_eff = sqrt(V_forced^2 + V_buoyant(g)^2) y la escala de de Ris (V_f ~ (k*rho*c)^(-1) para sólidos delgados)

hardware: Modelado CFD Multifísico (PSI-117 / PSI-142) acoplado con datos de FLEX-2 (PSI-68), CFI (PSI-39) y CFI-G (PSI-159)
key_findings: Tal como demostró PSI-117 para flujos convectivos de 3-8 cm/s, la velocidad boyante propia de la gravedad lunar (0.16g) y marciana (0.38g) no es suficiente para soplar la llama fría (que requiere >20 cm/s), sino que estira la zona NTC en una pluma ascendente donde se acumulan hidroperóxidos y se dispara la reignición secundaria a llama caliente
Predecir si la convección natural débil de la Luna y Marte barre la nube de llama fría o si, por el contrario, concentra peróxidos RO2 en la estela superior provocando reignición explosiva
modifications: En almacenes de solventes, laboratorios e invernaderos lunares/marcianos, mantener extracción forzada >25 cm/s o inertización con CO2/N2 tras cualquier conato líquido para impedir la reignición por pluma boyante de llama fría

hardware: Spacelab USML-1 (Space Shuttle Columbia STS-50) / 10 cm cylindrical chamber with CO2 laser heating (CT) and an immersed heater (CF) + IR thermography and PIV

name: PSI-117: Effect of External Thermo-Convective Perturbation on Cool Flame Dynamics: A Multiphysics Multidimensional CFD Analysis
hardware: Multidimensional multiphysics CFD simulation validated with orbital data from FLEX (PSI-69) and counterflow (PSI-142)
key_findings: A moderate convective perturbation accumulates intermediate species (peroxides and hydroperoxides) in the wake downstream of the droplet, which can cause an explosive secondary reignition to a hot flame, while an intense vortex breaks the NTC envelope and extinguishes the cool flame
Determine how multidimensional asymmetries induced by external convective flows or droplet interaction change cool-flame stability and trigger hot reignition
modifications: Avoid sudden ventilation pulses over post-extinction hydrocarbon vapour clouds, since the convective wake concentrates RO2/H2O2 radicals and triggers secondary hot reignition

key_findings: Established the unified four-branch S-curve flammability regimes, showing that the cool-flame branch survives strain rates and radiative losses at which the hot flame collapses

name: PSI-181: Structure and Properties of Pb-Sn and Lead-Free Sn-Ag-Cu Solders in Terrestrial vs. Microgravity under Extreme Temperatures
hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG - In-Space Soldering Investigation ISSI PSI-77) + cryogenic/elevated thermal cycling on Earth
key_findings: Joints soldered in microgravity retain large gas voids (porosity up to 5-10x higher than in 1 g), which reduces the effective electrical/thermal conduction section, creates Joule hot spots (risk of wire pyrolysis/ignition) and accelerates thermomechanical fracture under cryogenic cycling
Evaluate how the lack of buoyancy in microgravity traps flux vapour bubbles inside Pb-Sn and Sn-Ag-Cu solder joints, affecting electrical resistance, heat transfer and failure at extreme temperatures
modifications: Use solder wire without a volatile flux core, or apply vacuum/ultrasonic degassing during in-orbit electronic repairs (in-space manufacturing/repair), to avoid trapped pores that create hot spots and electrical ignition
Prefer doped SAC formulations with intermetallic control for lunar missions with cryogenic cycling
